text.p: CBOT wheat rebounded from Friday's losses and crude oil gained slightly, while gold and base metals eased on world markets. The CRB index closed 0.11 higher at 240.46.
METALS - Base metals closed lower on the London Metals Exchange despite a minor recovery in the afternoon which partly retraced heavy losses from aggressive fund selling earlier.

Flagship three months copper ended the session at $2,278 per tonne, a decline of $58, having bounced from a low of $2,264. But prices were still vulnerable to $2,250, or even $2,200, before resuming an upwards course, some analysts said.
Aluminium was similarly off its lows but still substantially weaker at $1,583, a decline of $41, after it sank below the $1,600 mark early in the day.

Some traders said the fund sell-off was sparked by losses sustained by aluminium futures on the Tokyo TOCOM exchange amid speculative selling. Others noted the selling appeared to be distress sale by funds caught out in other markets.
The start of daily LME stock reporting was said by most traders to have had little effect.
Zinc, which showed a stocks rise of 5,000 tonnes, was sold down sharply by the funds and ran into stop-loss selling. It ended $20 lower at $1,247.
Tin, which had plummeted by $200 to a near two-year low during the midday trading session, pared half of its losses, ending $100 weaker at $5,720.
Nickel, however, ended near its lows and finished $180 weaker at $7,290.
Lead prices finished $19 lower at $650, having bounced from a low of $636. Alloy was down $30 at $1,485.

WHEAT - CBOT wheat rebounded from Friday's sharply lower close to jump over one-half its daily trading limit in most contracts by Monday's closing bell. Concerns about delays in the seeding of the U.S. spring wheat crop and talk of potential damage to portions of the U.S. winter wheat crop from this week's cold weather, were cited as key catalysts for the gains, traders said. CBOT wheat closed 8-3/4 to 11-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 8-3/4 at $3.80-1/2 a bushel.

NYMEX OIL - NYMEX crude prices ended higher after Interprovincial Pipe Line (IPL) said that a power outage in Minnesota hit three of its pumping stations and took out a million barrels per day of througput from its pipeline. The positive settlement was the first in five sessions, with May crude ending 11 cents up at $19.23 a barrel.

GOLD - COMEX gold futures ended lower but other New York precious metals futures ended higher on light volumes. COMEX June gold ended down $0.60 at $351.00 an ounce after dipping to an early low at $349.40 on some trade selling, which was met by fund buying, dealers said.
